context: Add a Herdr adapter with explicit capability probing and canonical Bossmode herdr create and herdr close operations. Persist reservation intent before the external call, persist the exact returned worker and native-session identity afterward, and make close idempotent. Decision gate: if the installed Herdr CLI cannot expose a stable identity that survives pane movement and name reuse, creation may land but automatic deletion must remain blocked pending an approved runtime contract.
description: Make Herdr worker creation and cleanup symmetric. Bossmode must reserve ownership before invoking Herdr, bind the returned immutable live identity, reconcile that identity before every prompt or close, and close only workers it can prove it created. Existing externally created workers remain attachable but non-owned.

anti_patterns.dont: Close a worker using only a stored worker name or pane ID
anti_patterns.instead: Reconcile the immutable live worker and native-session identity against the creation receipt
anti_patterns.why: Names and panes can be reused or moved

anti_patterns.dont: Create a worker before reserving the owned-resource record
anti_patterns.instead: Persist intent first and reconcile incomplete reservations at startup
anti_patterns.why: A crash would leave an untracked resource

anti_patterns.dont: Hide unsupported Herdr capability behind best-effort cleanup
anti_patterns.instead: Fail the decision gate and keep closeout incomplete
anti_patterns.why: Best effort can delete the wrong worker or leak one silently

preserves.behavior: A missing already-owned worker makes retirement idempotently complete only after identity evidence excludes name reuse.
Bossmode never approves trust or permission dialogs.
Externally attached workers are never closed unless a later explicit ownership-adoption protocol is approved.
Live Herdr state remains authoritative for external worker identity and ownership.

prior_art.concept: reconcile before prompt or lifecycle action
